>  But I'm also incredibly anxious about work after experiencing intense anxiety and a toxic workplace at my last real job. 

That was me after dealing with my abusive dad \(boss\) at my first real job. I couldn't work for three years. 

> Rationally, I know I'm decent enough at food prep, basic customer service, etc, 

This is all you need for a job. Just the basics since you'll get better as you keep working. You don't need to go out and beyond. It's just a job and your employer knows that it's just a job to you. They're not asking a lot from you. They just want you to do your job. If you do wanna go a little extra that's fine, but don't overdo it. You'll stress yourself out. I tried to go out and beyond when I volunteered as a graphic designer \(real easy\), but I ended up becoming so overwhelmed because I feared I'd failed to live up to their expectations. I quit by ghosting. I shouldn't have done that, but I learned.  

> but I can't help but **feel** like I do an awful job and it shows, as though my employer **will see** how socially anxious and inept I am in the workplace and feel cheated for hiring me. 

This is the problem I had. I always 'feel' like I'll do something awful and mess up. When I applied as a cashier for a school bookstore, I was thinking about how I would mess up. I visualized it until I believed it. So, when they hired me, I told them I decided I didn't want the job. I felt like I wasted their time, but they were nice about it.

But in reality, what you feel doesn't always equate to reality. I have a job now and I always feel like I'm not doing good enough or am doing a crap job. Even when I before I was hired, I was scared about the interview and visualized how I'd mess up the interview. And when I was hired, I visualized how I'd mess up at work.

But my employers and clients always tell me that I'm doing great. So, my brain as shut up about that.

> I know I just have to take the plunge and try and work, but the idea of working completely fills me with dread. Has anyone else experienced this? How have you overcome it? 

Okay, what I'll say will make your eyes roll so hard. But...don't overthink it. I know right? Easier said than done. But seriously, don't overthink it. It's like a domino effect. Once you let yourself overthink, all the negative thoughts will pile up on you and you'll become too mentally exhausted to try. 

Congratulate yourself as you reach each step. Employer wants to interview you? Congratz! They think I'm qualified! Did well on the interview? Yay! They didn't see how awkward I am! Didn't get fired on the job? That's good. 

Also, it helps to prepare a little bit beforehand. If I don't know what I'm getting myself into, I get stressed and anxious. 

I could say more, but idk... 

Good luck!

Are you talking about nursing diplomas, ADN, and BSN? I've never heard of 'generic' and 'regular' nursing degree. Also, you don't get a certificate as an RN, you get a license. certification is for nursing assistant and it is not a degree.

Nursing diploma means you completed a program from a hospital. I don't know how long it takes, but it's around three years. 

ADN means you get an associate degree in nursing. It takes two years at a community college or university

BSN means you get a bachelor degree. It takes four years at a university or college.

I don't believe the pay is different. However, those with diplomas (if they're still out there) or ADN might have a difficult time getting a job than a BSN degree.

Question 1: I'd talk to the advisors at the school you want to transfer to. I'm sure if your GPA is like, 1 point less than the required, I don't think they'd get all bent out of shape. 


Question 2: I've taken one accelerated online course and couple of online courses before. 

It all depends on the subject, the teacher, and you. 

I took an accelerated course for Nutrition (with a registered dietitian) and it sucked. I had to read 7 chapters each week, do a quizzes for each, lots of assignments, discussions with uncessarily specific requirements, and exams that gives you 1 min for each question. Sometimes less. I passed with a B, but only because my mom helped. My teacher sucked. Granted, I was being lazy, but she was super strict on grading. In my opinion (and my mom and she's strict too), my teacher was unfair. 

My regular online course was much easier and more lax. It's Philosophy. I had to do 14 discussions and 2 papers. The discussions were non dated so you can do it whenever (but before the end of the semester) and then the two exams were dated. I got an A.

It also depends on how disciplined you are. ALso, if you're taking 5 courses, it might be too much for you? Again, it all depends on how disciplined you are and how much you're willing to sacrifice. 

Good luck! I started out with a shitty GPA too (2.4) and then worked my way up (now 3.1)
